transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling after your surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! I'm feeling okay, thank you for asking. I do have a few questions about my recovery. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're looking to get back to gardening. According to our guidance, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. Just remember to take it easy and be gentle with your eyes. Also, be careful not to get water in your eyes, especially in the first month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you! That's good to know. I have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're looking to use your eye drops for dry eyes. You should continue to use them as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you! Another question I have is that I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's severe or you're also experiencing significant pain, redness, and pain in the eye, we may need to assess it further. Mild sensitivity to light can be managed with sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to be a bit blurry in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks so much for all the information, Dora. I don't have any more questions right now. I really appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions. Now, I just want to check with you: do you feel like all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I feel like all my questions have been answered. Thanks again for your help!

verdict.label: pass
